purpose: Context-specific comparative regeneration evidence. Missing cells mean not profiled, not absence. Different endpoints are never numeric rankings.

cases.headline: Adult retinal neuron regeneration
cases.repair: Injured Müller glia can reprogram into proliferating progenitors, produce replacement retinal neurons, and support recovery of visual function in studied injury models.
cases.boundary: This does not establish that adult human retinas regenerate neurons spontaneously or that fish programs can simply be transplanted into human cells.

sources.title: Lenkowski & Raymond, Progress in Retinal and Eye Research (2014)

cases.functional: Visual recovery reported in zebrafish injury models

cases.headline: Reprogramming with an experimental intervention
cases.context: Adult mouse models of retinal degeneration
cases.repair: Blocking extracellular PROX1 transfer encouraged some Müller glia to adopt a regenerative program and produce retinal neurons, with delayed vision loss in mice.
cases.boundary: Untreated adult mouse retina does not normally reproduce the robust zebrafish response. Mouse visual improvements do not prove human efficacy or permanent recovery.
cases.functional: Improvement or delayed loss in experimental mouse visual assays

cases.headline: Functional endogenous replacement unestablished
cases.context: Adult human retina; clinical and tissue evidence
cases.repair: Human Müller glia have supportive functions and show injury responses, but spontaneous regeneration of functional retinal neurons sufficient to restore lost vision has not been demonstrated in living humans.
cases.boundary: Lack of demonstrated clinical regeneration is not proof that human retinal cells lack all latent plasticity. Human donor-tissue markers and preclinical interventions are not treatments.

sources.title: Huang et al., American Journal of Pathology (2026)

cases.functional: No established patient-level regeneration of functional retinal neurons
cases.origin: No proven robust spontaneous neuron replacement

cases.headline: Cardiac muscle can regenerate after resection
cases.context: Adult zebrafish after partial ventricular resection
cases.repair: Preexisting differentiated cardiomyocytes partly dedifferentiate and proliferate to form regenerated myocardium after experimental injury.
cases.boundary: The study does not imply adult human hearts can rebuild an equivalent mass of muscle after a heart attack.
cases.functional: Tissue regeneration studied; do not equate with human cardiac recovery

cases.headline: A short neonatal regeneration window
cases.context: Neonatal mice: 1 day versus 7 days after birth
cases.studyType: Peer-reviewed primary animal study; replication has depended on model and injury details
cases.repair: A 2011 mouse study reported substantial heart repair after partial resection at postnatal day one, with regenerative capacity diminished by day seven.
cases.boundary: This cannot be assigned to adult mice. Later studies have raised questions about variability, scarring, and experimental methods.

sources.title: A systematic analysis of neonatal mouse heart regeneration, Journal of Molecular and Cellular Cardiology (2014)

cases.functional: Repair reported in a specific neonatal injury model

cases.headline: Slow cardiomyocyte turnover, not full heart regrowth
cases.context: Adult human hearts studied through radiocarbon birth dating
cases.repair: Human cardiomyocytes undergo measurable low-level renewal across adulthood; the published model estimated turnover that decreases with age.
cases.boundary: Background cell turnover must not be described as replacement of a large myocardial infarct or restoration of fully functioning heart muscle after major injury.
cases.functional: Background turnover measured; not clinical myocardial regeneration

cases.headline: Neural stem cells expand during spinal cord regrowth
cases.repair: Axolotl neural stem cells expand in an organized way during regeneration of missing spinal cord regions, with planar cell polarity identified as a regulator.
cases.boundary: Cell expansion and tissue replacement in salamanders do not establish restored motor function in humans or a shared ready-to-use molecular therapy.
cases.functional: Anatomical spinal cord regeneration demonstrated; functional claims depend on specific assays

cases.headline: Adult central axons face strong regeneration limits
cases.context: Adult mouse and other mammalian spinal cord injury experiments
cases.studyType: Peer-reviewed mechanistic review of animal studies
cases.repair: Adult mammalian spinal cord neurons show limited spontaneous long-distance axon regeneration after severe injury; experimental strategies seek to improve growth and connections.
cases.boundary: This is not a claim that all spinal circuits lack plasticity. Neural sprouting, compensation, and function are different endpoints from replacing missing cord tissue.

sources.title: Muramatsu et al., International Journal of Molecular Sciences (2020)

cases.functional: Limited spontaneous structural regeneration in adult injury models

cases.headline: Clinical function can improve without full regrowth
cases.studyType: NIH clinical information plus randomized human trial
cases.repair: Recovery can occur through spared connections, protection, rehabilitation, and plasticity. Reliable rebuilding of severed human spinal cord pathways is not established as a treatment.
cases.boundary: Do not equate functional gains with anatomically regenerated spinal cord tissue. A 2025 anti-Nogo-A trial did not meet its overall primary endpoint.

sources.title: Anti-Nogo-A NG101 cervical SCI phase 2b trial, Lancet Neurology (2025)

cases.functional: Some patient recovery occurs, not proof of regenerated severed pathways

cases.headline: Regrowth of complex multi-tissue limbs
cases.studyType: Peer-reviewed primary single-cell study with prior lineage-tracing evidence
cases.repair: Cells assemble in a blastema and coordinate limb regrowth. Single-cell studies reveal multiple contributing populations, including fibroblast-like progenitors; regeneration does not require all cells to become pluripotent.
cases.boundary: A blastema is not one universal cell type, and salamander limb regeneration cannot be extrapolated to human limb regrowth.

sources.title: Kragl et al., Nature (2009): Tissue-origin memory during axolotl limb regeneration

cases.functional: Complex anatomical tissue regrowth, not a human outcome

cases.headline: Distal digit tip regeneration depends on nail region
cases.repair: Mouse distal digit tips can regenerate in a location-restricted manner; Wnt-responsive nail epithelial stem-cell signaling helps coordinate regrowth.
cases.boundary: Regeneration of the distal tip is not equivalent to regrowth of an entire finger, hand, or limb, and depends on tissue and injury location.
cases.functional: Anatomical regrowth within distal digit-tip model

cases.headline: Some distal fingertips can regrow
cases.context: Pediatric case series with selected distal fingertip injuries
cases.repair: A 1979 clinical report described restoration of fingertip contour and nail after selected distal injuries in four children. Outcomes depend on injury location and context.
cases.boundary: A small historical clinical series does not establish human limb regeneration or guarantee healing in other injuries. This atlas does not recommend specific wound-care procedures.

sources.title: Digit Tip Injuries: Current Treatment and Future Regenerative Paradigms (2019)

cases.functional: Favorable restoration documented in selected cases
cases.clinical: Observed clinical cases; not a standard regeneration drug
